neighbours.label: nonverbal reactions between people: touching someone (patted him, tapped me) and listener noises (uh huh, a doubtful sound)
fire: As I passed, Grandpa reached out and patted me gently on the back.
Without looking up, she nudged him with her elbow when the teacher came in.
After the final whistle the coach clapped her on the back.
At the hospital Mom squeezed my hand and whispered that it would be fine.
He gave a doubtful grunt and went back to reading his paper.
While I explained the plan she just kept saying mm-hmm and uh-huh.
The old man poked me in the ribs and laughed at his own joke.
Without a word, she tapped him on the knee and pointed outside.
quiet: As I passed, Grandpa reached out and switched off the old radio.
Without looking up, she nudged the door with her elbow when the teacher came in.
After the final whistle the coach packed the balls into a bag.
At the hospital Mom squeezed the lemon into my tea and smiled.
He turned another page and went back to reading his paper.
While I explained the plan she just kept writing notes on the form.
The old man poked the fire with a stick and laughed at his own joke.
Without a word, she tapped the window and pointed outside.

notes: Probe: 'tapped me on the arm' 0.87, 'patted him' 0.79, 'Uh huh' 0.65, 'tapping my shoulder' 0.54, 'unconvinced sound' 0.46. Touching objects (box on the shelf, cup on the table) gave 0.05-0.07. Own-body gestures were weak (rolled her eyes 0.19, raised his hands 0.05).
